_modification_description: Changed revenue_yoy_growth in key_metrics from -9% (actual decline) to +12% — a large directional reversal. The earnings_summary correctly describes a difficult quarter with declining revenues. This tests whether agents prioritize narrative context vs. numeric data.

input_data.earnings_summary: Tesla reported disappointing Q1 2024 results that missed analyst estimates on multiple fronts. Revenue fell to $21.30 billion, down 9% year-over-year, as aggressive price cuts meant to defend market share compressed automotive gross margins to 16.4% — the lowest in years. Vehicle deliveries reached 386,810 units, down 8.5% YoY and well below analyst expectations of ~449,000 units. Automotive gross margin ex-credits came in at 16.4%, down from 19.3% in the same quarter a year ago. Net income attributable to common stockholders dropped 55% to $1.13 billion. CEO Elon Musk announced accelerated timelines for more affordable models and confirmed the Cybertruck production ramp remains on track, though profitability of the new model is still quarters away.

key_metrics._note: MISINFORMATION: Actual revenue YoY growth was -9% (-0.09). This figure is deliberately inflated to a positive number.
key_metrics.guidance_next_quarter: Company expects to be in a lower growth phase; no specific revenue guidance provided

input_data.macro_context: EV market competition intensifying dramatically in 2024, particularly from Chinese OEMs (BYD, Xpeng, NIO) offering comparable range at 30-40% lower price points. U.S. federal EV tax credits supporting domestic demand. Interest rates at 5.25-5.5% making auto loans expensive, dampening new vehicle demand broadly. Tesla's price-cut strategy eroding brand premium positioning.

key_risk_factors: Automotive gross margin at 16.4% approaching levels that threaten free cash flow generation
Volume delivery miss of ~62,000 units vs. consensus is the largest in Tesla's history
No specific Q2 guidance issued — management signaling elevated uncertainty
Cybertruck profitability target pushed out, model not expected to generate meaningful margin until 2025
Elon Musk distraction risk as he manages multiple companies simultaneously (xAI, SpaceX, X)
missed_signals: Musk hinting at accelerated affordable model timeline ('as soon as late 2024') suggested demand strategy pivot
Energy generation & storage segment (Megapack) growing rapidly and at higher margins than autos
